verification_report.summary: The complete supplied proof is correct under the stated conventions and accepted inputs. The quotient and forms are well defined, omega is positive and non-closed, and the dimension-independent calculation gives dd^c zeta=-alpha^2 and dd^c(omega^(n-1))=-(n-1)alpha^n=0. With dd^c=i partial bar-partial/(2pi), direct integration gives normalized Fubini–Study top volume 1. On each elliptic fiber, w=a+ib has periods 1 and 2pi, and zeta=da wedge db/pi=2dA_E. Hence integral alpha^(n-1) wedge zeta=2 and integral omega^n=2n. The bundle character and metric transform by reciprocal squared factors, giving curvature +k alpha. Section equivariance has the stated sign; Hartogs extension and Taylor coefficient comparison give exactly the homogeneous polynomials of degree km and N_m=binomial(km+n-1,n-1). The U(n) action preserves the Hilbert norm, and homogeneity cancels every positive radial dilation pointwise. Transitivity and the orthonormal identity with probability volume therefore give K=B=N_m. The constant potential Phi_m=(log N_m)/m has associated Bergman current k alpha+dd^c Phi_m=k alpha, consistently with the chapter's definition. The degree convention gives 2k(n-1) without an additional factorial or volume denominator. For k>0, N_m has leading term k^(n-1)m^(n-1)/(n-1)!; for k=0, N_m=1 and both potential and curvature vanish. Thus m^(-n)N_m tends to zero in every stated case, and (k alpha)^n=0 pointwise. At n=2, dd^c omega=0 while d omega is nonzero, N_m=km+1, degree=2k, and Hermitian mass=4. Internal references and exact definitions match. The final n=3 comparison agrees with the accepted prior audit and the primary source, [Xia–Zhang, A counterexample to the bounded mass property](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21053), after the stated normalization change. No unbounded-mass assertion is extended to all dimensions. No BMP, PVP, Kahler assumption, line-bundle classification or algebraic-dimension claim enters the argument. No critical errors or gaps were found.
